summary:
Set 128 Session 2 of 3 ships Component A: the ORDERING RULES the shape from Session 1 protects, and the mechanized half of A4.

(1) A1-A3 WRITTEN WHERE THEY CAN BE OBEYED. The constitution's Step 5 now says targeted runs only (A1) and NO FULL SUITE BEFORE ANY CROSS-PROVIDER STAGE (A2) -- naming the path-aware critique as such a stage, which is stricter than treating the critique and the suite as one Step-8 block. A3 keeps a targeted spec at any layer legitimate (including a Layer 3 spec before a UAT walk) and puts "required portion" on `covers` rather than on running everything. The authoring guide carries the full statement with the operator rulings verbatim, the two incidents (Set 112 S3's 15 runs / 186 minutes; Set 127 S2's compressed step), and the superseded line-count formulation marked do-not-reintroduce.

(2) A4 WAS CONTRADICTED BY THE MACHINERY, NOT MERELY UNWRITTEN -- the finding that reshaped this session. The operator ruled that a post-suite fix to TESTS ONLY owes no re-verification (A4.1) and a post-suite fix to SHIPPED CODE owes a targeted remediation-review, not an open one (A4.2). But ANY post-verification edit moved `work_diff_sha256`, so a one-line test fix staled the stamped row and `close_session`'s backstop bought a full metered round. Writing A4 as prose would have shipped a rule the code actively defeated. This was surfaced to the operator as an education-mode brief before any implementation: they were inclined to exclude test paths from the work-diff digest, asked for the risks, and switched on reading them (time-blindness, invisible test DELETION -- which collides with Set 118 -- denylist fail-open, no audit trail, and A4.2 left unmechanized).

(3) WHAT SHIPPED. `ai_router/post_round_delta.py` classifies the delta since the session's recorded round as no-change / test-only / shipped-code / unknown, with `unknown` owing a review exactly as shipped-code does. Neither half of the question is invented: "what changed" is a tree-to-tree diff under the freshness exclusions, and "what is a test" is `run_of_record`'s new per-suite `tests` allowlist beside `covers` (L-125-1 -- `test-fixtures/` and `scripts/` are deliberately NOT test surfaces, because they stage what Layer 3 asserts). `record_round_completed` now snapshots `worktreeTreeAtCompletion` on EVERY completed round, because `discoveryBaselineTree` is taken pre-round and over-reports; it stays the named fallback and the verdict says which anchor it used. `validate_stamped_row`'s freshness check gains the A4.1 exemption -- reached ONLY on a digest mismatch, exempting freshness and nothing else -- and the close backstop ledgers every exemption as `a4-test-only-exemption`, so a close that settled under A4.1 is distinguishable in the record from one that re-verified.

(4) THE OPERATOR ISSUED A STANDING GUIDANCE-CEILING AUTHORIZATION MID-SESSION. Writing A1-A3 put the constitution 128 tokens over its 4,000-token preload ceiling, and the corpus has sat at 99-100% of every ceiling since Set 085 S2, so every unrelated set touching a preload file pays a slimming tax. I had begun compressing three unrelated sections when the operator authorized exceeding the ceilings until Set 121 lands. Recorded durably in three places (`docs/guidance-lifecycle.md` verbatim with three conditions, the matching `router-config.yaml` paragraph, and an explicit RETIREMENT obligation added to Set 121 Session 4 Step 3) and the three unrelated compressions were REVERTED, so the constitution's diff is the A1-A4 rules and nothing else. Raise-to-fit: 4,200 and 12,200 against measurements of 4,084 and 11,985, so the gate still reports honestly and CI stays green.

(5) VERIFICATION FOUND FOUR MAJORS ACROSS FIVE ROUNDS, AND THE LAST TWO WERE ONE CLASS. Round 1 (2-lens discovery): both lenses independently found that A4.2 was only REPORTED, not implemented -- I had scoped it back, and my authoring-guide prose asserted behaviour the code did not have. The verifiers were right and my reasoning was wrong: the baseline is RECORDED, not assumed. Round 2 (supplementary, run BEFORE remediating) found the more valuable defect: `classify_delta` reused `work_diff_binding_paths`, which unions ALL currently-untracked files, so an unchanged untracked file captured in the anchor tree was re-reported as a post-round change -- denying A4.1 to precisely the sessions that create a new file, the common shape. Rounds 3 and 4 then found the same CLASS twice: the backstop MIRRORED the CLI's remediation-review phase piece by piece and each round found a different missing piece (first the cross-round ledger and fix-verdict coverage, then the phased evidence exclusions). At the bound I stopped to the operator with three options and they authorized ONE round for the CLASS fix rather than the instance: `verify_session.build_phase_round_inputs` now assembles the phase once and both callers read it. Round 5 (operator-authorized): VERIFIED, 4 fix verdicts accepted, 0 rejected, 0 findings.

(6) FALSIFIERS, AND TWO PROBES THAT MATTERED. 15 cases in `test_post_round_delta.py` plus 4 A4 tests in `test_close_backstop.py`, all planting real edits in real git repos rather than reading predicates. Three mutation probes: widening the classifier failed 6 of 13 cases; dropping the phased exclusions failed the bookkeeping test; and a probe pinning the exemption predicate to "granted" initially survived ALL of them -- a real gap, closed with a both-directions assertion before the change shipped, after which the re-probe fails. The class fix carries a STRUCTURAL assertion that fails if the backstop ever assembles a second spelling of the phase, which is what makes a third gap unreachable rather than merely unobserved.

(7) THE SET DOGFOODED ITS OWN RULE LIVE. The full pytest run returned one failure: a structural test asserting `verify_session.run`'s source names `PHASED_EVIDENCE_SET_EXCLUDES`, which the class fix legitimately moved. The fix was test-only, and `post_round_delta` classified it as exactly that -- A4.1, owes no re-verification -- on the session that shipped the rule. A4.1 exempts re-verification, not suite freshness, so pytest was re-run in full and recorded: 4,162 passed / 9 skipped.

reason.specifics: Session 3 re-authors other sets' specs under the skeleton and the ordering this session wrote, so it needs the context of WHY each rule reads as it does -- particularly that A3 puts the required portion on `covers` (which is what let this session owe pytest only) and that A4 is keyed on what changed, never on how much. SCOPE CHANGE RATIFIED BY THE OPERATOR THIS SESSION and journalled in decisions.jsonl: Session 3 now handles FOUR unstarted specs, not one. Step 2 stays substantive -- re-author 118 to the new skeleton AND the new ordering. Step 3 additionally performs the MECHANICAL restructuring of 113, 121 and 122 and then re-admits all four. Measured: every one of those 14 sessions has the identical malformation (a 5-step session whose step 5 compresses verify + full suite + close), and the fix is to replace that one step with three, giving 7 steps and exactly N=3 work steps, so no sessionSizeException is needed anywhere. Session 3 must make that spec edit itself: doing it in Session 2 would have staled a VERIFIED round and, under this set's own A4.2, bought another review. Session 3 is set-terminal, so it also owes the path-aware critique (the set declares `pathAwareCritique: required`), change-log.md, and the Step 9 guidance review. Same seat and effort; verification must keep routing to a different effective provider than anthropic -- gpt-5.5 returned four real Majors here and none were noise.

residuals.item: The standing operator authorization to exceed the guidance preload ceilings (2026-08-12) is ACTIVE and must be retired.
residuals.note: Recorded in three places so it cannot be lost: the verbatim quote and its three conditions in docs/guidance-lifecycle.md, the matching paragraph beside the ceilings in ai_router/router-config.yaml, and an explicit retirement obligation written into Set 121's own spec. An accommodation nobody retires is how a temporary one becomes the norm, which is why the expiry names a step rather than a hope.

residuals.item: A5 -- how 'the required portion' resolves per MODULE -- is still open, and the operator has now scheduled it.
residuals.owner: a new Set 129, ratified by the operator this session
residuals.note: The operator supplied a proposal (C:\Users\Public\multi-module-retesting-rules.md) and authorized a new set rather than a fourth session here, since this set's spec declares A5 out of scope. Independent reviews were commissioned from gpt-5.6-sol and gemini-3.1-pro and both landed on the same conclusion: adopt the suite-owned input-set abstraction, REJECT the contract/mock/lock machinery as premature for a framework whose consumer repos have not demonstrated that architecture, and treat the proposal's claim that skipping an unaffected suite is 'provably redundant rather than a risk trade-off' as false given non-hermetic suites and a `covers` list that is a path prefix, not a dependency graph. Set 129 is NOT yet authored -- Session 3 should name it as A5's owner when it retires the source-of-record note.

residuals.item: The A4.2 delta-scoped backstop round is shipped but has never fired in production.
residuals.owner: the first session that fixes shipped code after its full suite
residuals.note: It is covered by four falsifiers and a structural assertion, and its bound arithmetic is asserted against a hand-built ledger, but every one of those exercises it through the test harness rather than a live close. Worth watching the first time a real session takes that path.

checklist.note: Three transitions left a record with no post inside their own window, all three operator stops. The gate counts RECORDS, not stops, and the two verification-reduction records (the A4.1/A4.2 rule and its mechanization depth) were journalled back-to-back from ONE operator stop with one post before it -- the same structural shape Session 1 recorded for three test-run records written seconds apart. The third is the guidance-ceiling authorization, which the operator volunteered mid-step rather than my stopping for it, so no window opened before the record landed. The gate is ADVISORY (Set 116 S3 ruling) and is NOT waived here: a waiver needs an operator attestation and none was sought, so the omission is recorded rather than excused. The observation Session 1 offered for Step 9 now has a second data point and generalizes: a sanctioned writer that appends a gate-visible record could post the checklist itself from the line after its append -- decision_journal here, run_of_record for the suite records -- exactly as verify_session already does for round transitions. Offered for Step 9, NOT scope taken here.
